id_and_class.summary: Nino Kadić accepts that micro-subjects cannot combine into a macro-subject, so he builds a panpsychism that never needs them to. Each fundamental microsubject has an intrinsic bare point of view, and its rich experiential content is fixed by its relations to other microsubjects in the same causal structure, so one microsubject (or, on one version, every one) can have a full human experience. Inspired by Leibniz's monads, the view avoids both subject-combination and emergence.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Human Experience as Relationally Constituted Microsubjects

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a bare perspective intrinsic to every fundamental simple; the qualitative richness of a human experience belongs to a microsubject through its relations to other microsubjects.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Phenomenal structure mirrors causal structure: the causal organization of the brain determines, relationally, the phenomenal character of the microsubject or microsubjects within it.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (Kadić explicitly rejects emergence and replaces it with relational constitution)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: There is no macrosubject over and above microsubjects. What we call a human subject is a microsubject whose relationally constituted experience presents as a single ‘I’; on the global version, many qualitatively identical microsubjects each say ‘I’ at once and are experienced as one.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Following Michael Tye's distinction, consciousness-as-such is intrinsic, sharp and determinate, while experiential content is relational, vague and indeterminate. A microsubject can have quark-type experience in isolation and quite different experience as part of a particular causal structure.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Fundamental microsubjects with intrinsic points of view and an indefinite range of relational properties, organized in causal structures; no complex higher-level subjects.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Metaphysical argument, drawing on Leibniz and on the representational theory of experience.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Hierarchically organized microsubjects individuated by their internal states, each able to reflect all others, with (on the Leibnizian versions) a dominant one at the top.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal consciousness, the unity of the self, and the combination problem.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Microphenomenal structuralism: all microsubjects in a relevant causal structure relationally determine the phenomenal character of one microsubject, or of all of them, so that it amounts to a full human experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: In the dynamic version, which microsubject is dominant can switch from moment to moment, probably in step with brain processes; if it is removed, another takes over.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Microsubjects exist everywhere; human-level experience exists in the microsubject or microsubjects that the brain's causal structure singles out.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity comes from dominance by a single microsubject (dynamic version) or from the qualitative identity of many microsubjects (global version), never from microsubjects merging.
core_claims_and_evidence: The subject combination problem is probably insurmountable, and Coleman argues that merging subjects is incoherent, so panpsychism should avoid combination entirely.
Static monadic panpsychism fails because the brain would lose its experience if its one permanently dominant microsubject were damaged.
Dynamic monadic panpsychism lets any microsubject take the dominant role, which handles that objection but requires a principle for individuating the dominant one.
Global monadic panpsychism makes every microsubject in the structure have the full human experience, which Kadić admits is the hardest version to defend.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Static and dynamic versions must explain how the dominant microsubject relates to the others and how it is individuated. Siddharth and Bhojraj, who defend a similar Leibnizian panpsychism, deny that a single dominant microsubject can be sharply fixed and reject the global version.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Kadić concedes that monadic panpsychism faces unique difficulties, especially the counterintuitive result in the global version that many ‘Ninos’ in one brain share the same experience.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Kadić argues the view faces a less worrying set of objections than combinatory or emergentist panpsychism; he keeps Leibniz's structure of monads while dropping the soul-monad and divine orchestration.

AI_consciousness.rationale: If phenomenal structure mirrors causal structure, it follows that a suitably organized artificial system could give its microsubjects rich experience, though Kadić's account here does not address AI.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: The microsubjects persist, but the human experience they host is constituted by their relations within the brain's causal structure, so it follows from the view that this experience ends when that structure does.
